pointers.sentence: The factory's docstring says its request can be passed to any view function as though the view had been reached through a URLconf (`django/test/client.py:RequestFactory`).
`HttpRequest.resolver_match` stays `None`, and the test passes the view its URL's arguments (`django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler.resolve_request`).

`RequestFactory.json_encoder` is `DjangoJSONEncoder` by default; `RequestFactory.cookies` starts as an empty `SimpleCookie`; `RequestFactory.errors` is each request's `"wsgi.errors"` (`django/test/client.py:RequestFactory.__init__`).
The defaults are laid over these keys, and the request's own over the defaults (`django/test/client.py:RequestFactory._base_environ`).
Every method ends in `RequestFactory.generic`, whose keys `RequestFactory.request` makes into a `WSGIRequest` (`django/test/client.py:RequestFactory.generic`).
A dictionary under any other content type, or given to `options`, is sent as its `str` (`django/test/client.py:RequestFactory._encode_json`, `django/test/client.py:RequestFactory._encode_data`).
A dictionary under any other content type, or given to `options`, is sent as its `str` (`django/test/client.py:RequestFactory._encode_json`, `django/test/client.py:RequestFactory._encode_data`).

A key's value of `None` is refused with a `TypeError` asking whether an empty string or no value was meant (`django/test/client.py:encode_multipart`, `django/test/client.py:encode_file`); the parser's side is [Multipart parsing and upload handlers](../http/uploads.md).

A key's value of `None` is refused with a `TypeError` asking whether an empty string or no value was meant (`django/test/client.py:encode_multipart`, `django/test/client.py:encode_file`); the parser's side is [Multipart parsing and upload handlers](../http/uploads.md).
Its docstring's reason: network data cannot be sought or read past its length, and a view should do nothing under the test client that would fail in real life (`django/test/client.py:FakePayload`).
`AsyncRequestFactory.request` wraps the payload in a `LimitedStream` of its length, so a long read returns what there is (`django/test/client.py:AsyncRequestFactory.request`).

Each is put in lower case with `"_"` as `"-"`: `ASGIRequest` drops a header with an underscore (CVE-2026-3902), and the comment's reason is not to break tests that give names in that form ([Making the request: `WSGIRequest` and `ASGIRequest`](../http/request.md#from-an-asgi-scope), `django/test/client.py:AsyncRequestFactory.generic`).
